long_biography.plain_text:
An interest in horses drew Swiss architect Alain Meylan to the Alpilles, where he first bought a former tenant farmer's house. He then acquired the adjoining historic residence and olive mill that became Le Mas de Chabran. With interior designer Liliana Atilova, he spent two years restoring the property before welcoming guests.

Their renovation preserved the old oil press within a vaulted reception room while introducing contemporary furniture and artworks. They expanded the collection through further restorations, retaining each building's existing character. At La Bergerie de Calabrun, the conversion kept the three original levels and incorporated a large natural rock into the living space.
